title: The eye and the heart
intro: Baba Taher, called *'Oryān* 'the Naked', was a wandering dervish of Hamadan in western Iran. The historian Ravandi tells that the Seljuk sultan Toghrul met him on a hill outside the city around 1055, got down from his horse, kissed his hand and asked for his blessing. His *dobeytis* – 'two-couplet' quatrains in a lighter, more singable metre than Khayyam's – were composed in the old dialect of the region, and shepherds, villagers and great singers have sung them for nine hundred years. They are printed here as they usually are today, in a Persian close to the standard language with a few dialect words. These six are among the best known: the eye and the heart, the beloved seen everywhere, and the pains and cures of love.

lines.fa: ز دست دیده و دل هر دو فریاد / که هر چه دیده بیند دل کند یاد
lines.r: ze dast-e dide vo del har do faryād / ke har che dide binad del konad yād
lines.en: Help! I cry out against my eyes and my heart, / for whatever the eye sees, the heart remembers.
lines.note: «از دست کسی فریاد» 'help against someone!' is still how Persian complains: «از دست تو!» 'oh, you!'.
words: help against…!, I cry out against… (lit. 'from the hand of')
lines.faV: ز دَستِ دیده و دِل هَر دو فَریاد / که هَر چه دیده بینَد دِل کُنَد یاد

lines.fa: بسازم خنجری نیشش ز فولاد / زنم بر دیده تا دل گردد آزاد
lines.r: besāzam khanjari nish-ash ze fulād / zanam bar dide tā del gardad āzād
lines.en: I'll make a dagger with a point of steel / and strike my eye, to set my heart free.
words: I will strike – the old present used as a future
lines.faV: بِسازَم خَنجَری نیشَش ز فولاد / زَنَم بَر دیده تا دِل گَردَد آزاد

lines.fa: به صحرا بنگرم صحرا ته وینم / به دریا بنگرم دریا ته وینم
lines.r: be sahrā bengaram sahrā ta vinam / be daryā bengaram daryā ta vinam
lines.en: When I look at the plain, I see you in the plain; / when I look at the sea, I see you in the sea.
words: you (as object) – dialect for تو را
lines.faV: به صَحرا بِنگَرَم صَحرا ته وینَم / به دَریا بِنگَرَم دَریا ته وینَم

lines.fa: به هر جا بنگرم کوه و در و دشت / نشان از قامت رعنا ته وینم
lines.r: be har jā bengaram kuh o dar o dasht / neshān az ghāmat-e ra'nā ta vinam
lines.en: Wherever I look – mountain, valley, plain – / I see a sign of your tall and graceful figure.
lines.faV: به هَر جا بِنگَرَم کوه و دَر و دَشت / نِشان اَز قامَتِ رَعنا ته وینَم

lines.fa: اگر دل دلبره دلبر کدامه / وگر دلبر دله دل را چه نامه
lines.r: agar del delbar-e delbar kodām-e / vagar delbar del-e del rā che nām-e
lines.en: If the heart is the beloved, then which is the beloved? / And if the beloved is the heart, what is the heart called?
words: is the beloved – dialect ـه for است
what is the name? – چه نام است
lines.faV: اَگَر دِل دِلبَره دِلبَر کُدامه / وَگَر دِلبَر دِله دِل را چه نامه

lines.fa: دل و دلبر به هم آمیته وینم / ندونم دل که و دلبر کدامه
lines.r: del o delbar be ham āmite vinam / nadunam del ke vo delbar kodām-e
lines.en: I see the heart and the beloved mingled into one; / I cannot tell which is the heart and which the beloved.
words: I don't know – ندانم (spoken Tehrani نمی‌دونم)
lines.faV: دِل و دِلبَر به هَم آمیته وینَم / نَدونَم دِل که و دِلبَر کُدامه

lines.fa: دلی دیرم خریدار محبت / کز او گرم است بازار محبت
lines.r: deli diram kharidār-e mohabbat / kaz u garm ast bāzār-e mohabbat
lines.en: I have a heart that buys love, / and it keeps love's market busy.
lines.faV: دِلی دیرَم خَریدارِ مُحَبَّت / کَز او گَرم اَست بازارِ مُحَبَّت

lines.fa: لباسی دوختم بر قامت دل / ز پود محنت و تار محبت
lines.r: lebāsi dukhtam bar ghāmat-e del / ze pud-e mehnat o tār-e mohabbat
lines.en: I have sewn a garment to fit my heart, / with a weft of suffering and a warp of love.
lines.note: تار و پود 'warp and weft' is the Persian for the very fabric of something: «تار و پود وجودم» 'every fibre of my being'.
lines.faV: لِباسی دوختَم بَر قامَتِ دِل / ز پودِ مِحنَت و تارِ مُحَبَّت

lines.fa: یکی درد و یکی درمان پسندد / یکی وصل و یکی هجران پسندد
lines.r: yeki dard o yeki darmān pasandad / yeki vasl o yeki hejrān pasandad
lines.en: One wants the pain and one the cure; / one wants union and one separation.
lines.faV: یِکی دَرد و یِکی دَرمان پَسَندَد / یِکی وَصل و یِکی هِجران پَسَندَد

lines.fa: من از درمان و درد و وصل و هجران / پسندم آنچه را جانان پسندد
lines.r: man az darmān o dard o vasl o hejrān / pasandam ānche rā jānān pasandad
lines.en: Of cure and pain, of union and parting, / I want whatever my beloved wants.
lines.faV: مَن اَز دَرمان و دَرد و وَصل و هِجران / پَسَندَم آنچه را جانان پَسَندَد

lines.fa: دلا خوبان دل خونین پسندند / دلا خون شو که خوبان این پسندند
lines.r: delā khubān del-e khunin pasandand / delā khun sho ke khubān in pasandand
lines.en: O heart, the beautiful love a bleeding heart; / so bleed, my heart, for that is what they love.
words: to turn to blood – to suffer deeply
lines.faV: دِلا خوبان دِلِ خونین پَسَندَند / دِلا خون شو که خوبان این پَسَندَند

lines.fa: متاع کفر و دین بی‌مشتری نیست / گروهی آن گروهی این پسندند
lines.r: matā'-e kofr o din bi-moshtari nist / goruhi ān goruhi in pasandand
lines.en: The goods of unbelief and of faith both find buyers: / some like that, and some like this.
lines.faV: مَتاعِ کُفر و دین بی‌مُشتَری نیست / گُروهی آن گُروهی این پَسَندَند

commentary:
**The images.** Baba Taher's world is small and concrete: the eye and the heart, the plain, the sea and the mountain, a dagger, a garment, a market. Out of these he makes the great themes of mystical love. The eye sees and the heart cannot forget, so the poet threatens to blind himself; the beloved is so present that he is seen in every landscape, and so close that lover and beloved can no longer be told apart. The heart is a buyer in love's market and wears a garment woven of love and suffering. The last two dobeytis are about surrender: the lover wants whatever the beloved wants, even pain – and if the beautiful like a bleeding heart, then bleed.

**The rhythm.** A *dobeyti* looks like a *robā'i* – four half-lines, rhyming in lines 1, 2 and 4 – but it has its own lighter metre, a short *hazaj*: *da-DUM-DUM-DUM da-DUM-DUM-DUM da-DUM-DUM*. Hear it in *be sah-rā ben-ga-ram sah-rā ta vi-nam*. It is the metre of folk song all over Iran, and Baba Taher's poems are more often sung than recited. Several repeat a word or two after the rhyme, a [[ردیف|radif]]: [[ته وینم|ta vinam]], [[محبت|mohabbat]], [[پسندد|pasandad]], [[پسندند|pasandand]].

**The grammar.** The dialect words are few and easy: [[دیرم|diram]] for [[دارم|dāram]], [[وینم|vinam]] for [[بینم|binam]], [[ته|ta]] for [[تو را|to rā]], [[آمیته|āmite]] for [[آمیخته|āmikhte]], [[ندونم|nadunam]] for [[ندانم|nadānam]]. The ending [[ـه|-e]] for [[است|ast]] – [[دلبره|delbar-e]] 'is the beloved', [[کدامه|kodām-e]] 'which is it?' – is exactly what you hear in spoken Tehrani Persian today. The first dobeyti in modern prose: [[از دست چشم و دلم فریاد، چون دل هر چه را چشم می‌بیند به یاد می‌آورد. خنجری با نوک فولادی می‌سازم و به چشمم می‌زنم تا دلم آزاد شود|az dast-e cheshm o del-am faryād, chon del har che rā cheshm mi-binad be yād mi-āvarad. khanjari bā nok-e fulādi mi-sāzam va be cheshm-am mi-zanam tā del-am āzād shavad]].

**Using it.** Baba Taher is the poet of ordinary people: his dobeytis are sung at weddings and in the mountains, and Iran's great classical singers have recorded them again and again. His tomb, a modern tower on a hill in Hamadan, is one of the city's landmarks. [[به صحرا بنگرم صحرا ته وینم|be sahrā bengaram sahrā ta vinam]] is the line people quote about a love they see everywhere, and [[گروهی آن گروهی این پسندند|goruhi ān goruhi in pasandand]] settles any argument about taste.
